abstract.para: In the System screen, configure the host name and the time synchronization servers.

textobject.phrase: Screenshot of the &agama; installer for &productname; &productnumber; showing the system settings page. It provides settings to configure the host name and adjust Network Time Protocol (NTP) time synchronization servers.

section.title: Setting the host name
section.para: Set the host name of the system in one of the following modes.

listitem.para: The host name is assigned with DHCP and may change after a reboot or network change. The transient host name agama is used for the installation.
Set a static host name. You can either use a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) or the host name part only.

important.title: Host name for registration
important.para: The host name is used for the registration with the &scc;. If you do not set a host name, your system will be registered with the transient host name agama. Even if the system is assigned a new host name later, it will not automatically get updated in the &scc;. Therefore setting host name is recommended.
To update the host name in the &scc; after registration, first change the system's host name. Then use &suseconnect; to deregister the system and register it again under the new host name.

tip.title: Identifying systems in the &scc;
tip.para: If you have multiple systems registered with the same host name in the &scc;, it is difficult to tell them apart. To identify a system, use its UUID. You can find it under Hardware information in the &scc; and on the system by running dmidecode -s system-uuid.

section.title: Setting time synchronization servers
section.para: The system time is set with the Network Time Protocol (NTP) to ensure the system time is always correct. Choose one of the following modes:

listitem.para: The system uses one of the default &suse; NTP servers 1.suse.pool.ntp.org to 3.suse.pool.ntp.org. If your system is behind a firewall, make sure that these servers are reachable from your network.
In the custom mode, you can configure the NTP servers to use. Use this option for air-gapped environments. Specify servers by host name, IP address or FQDN. Separate multiple entries with colons.

section.para: Click Accept to save your changes.
